claims.claim: Eusebius of Caesarea was a bishop of Caesarea in Palestine, born about 260 CE and died before 341 CE.
Eusebius became bishop of Caesarea around 313 CE.
Most of Eusebius's letters are lost, but his letters to Carpianus and Flacillus exist complete.
Eusebius was a prolific writer, biblical scholar, and apologist who lived approximately 260–339 CE.
Eusebius played a significant role in ecclesiastical politics in the eastern empire from his election as bishop of Caesarea around 313 until his death in 339.
Eusebius attended and assented to the decisions of the Council of Nicaea in 325, having been readmitted to communion after recanting his earlier views.
Eusebius was present at the Council of Tyre in 335 as an opponent of Athanasius.
Eusebius was one of the most influential thinkers of early Christianity, especially in his contributions to conceptions of Christian history, politics, and trinitarian theology.
Eusebius's intellectual formation at Caesarea in Palestine owed much to the influence of Pamphilus, who was martyred in 310.
